title: GitHub Actions: patterns comunes en workflows
excerpt: Recetas de workflows GitHub Actions para casos reales.
body:
## Estructura básica
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
```yaml
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20 }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
```

## Triggers comunes
```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
    paths-ignore: ['docs/**', '*.md']
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * *'    # daily 3AM UTC
  workflow_dispatch:        # manual
    inputs:
      env:
        description: 'Environment'
        required: true
        default: 'staging'
        type: choice
        options: [staging, production]
```

## Secrets
```yaml
steps:
  - name: Deploy
    env:
      API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
      DB_PASS: ${{ secrets.DB_PASS }}
    run: ./deploy.sh
```

Define secrets en repo settings.

## Matrix builds
```yaml
jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        node: [18, 20, 22]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: ${{ matrix.node }} }
```

9 combos (3 OS × 3 Node) → parallel.

## Caching
```yaml
- uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: ~/.npm
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
    restore-keys: |
      ${{ runner.os }}-npm-
```

Cacheia dependencies para speed.

## Conditional steps
```yaml
steps:
  - name: Deploy to prod
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    run: ./deploy-prod.sh
```

## Reusable workflows
### Defined workflow
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:
```yaml
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      env:
        required: true
        type: string
    secrets:
      api-token:
        required: true
```

### Called workflow
```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/deploy.yml
    with:
      env: production
    secrets:
      api-token: ${{ secrets.PROD_TOKEN }}
```

## Job dependencies
```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps: [...]

  deploy:
    needs: build   # runs after build succeeds
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps: [...]
```

## Environments (protection rules)
```yaml
deploy:
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://myapp.com
```

Requires manual approval (config en repo settings).

## Concurrency (prevent duplicate runs)
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: deploy-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Only one deploy per branch active.

## Docker build & push
```yaml
- uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
- uses: docker/login-action@v3
  with:
    username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USER }}
    password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASS }}
- uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
  with:
    context: .
    push: true
    tags: myapp:${{ github.sha }}, myapp:latest
    cache-from: type=gha
    cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
```

## Deploy a Cloud Foundry
```yaml
- name: Install CF CLI
  run: |
    curl -L 'https://packages.cloudfoundry.org/stable?release=linux64-binary&version=v8&source=github' | tar -zx
    sudo mv cf8 /usr/local/bin/cf

- name: Deploy
  env:
    CF_USER: ${{ secrets.CF_USER }}
    CF_PASS: ${{ secrets.CF_PASS }}
  run: |
    cf api https://api.cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com
    cf auth $CF_USER $CF_PASS
    cf target -o myorg -s prod
    cf push
```

## Notifications
### Slack
```yaml
- uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
  if: failure()
  with:
    status: ${{ job.status }}
    fields: repo,ref,commit
  env:
    SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
```

### Teams
HTTP POST to webhook.

## Common issues
### 'Secret not found'
- Not defined en repo settings
- Case-sensitive nombre
- No accessible en forks (default)

### 'Runner out of disk'
- Docker images acumulados
- `runs-on: ubuntu-latest-4-cores` (bigger runner)

### 'Workflow timeout'
- Default: 6 hours
- Increase: `timeout-minutes: 30`

### 'Cache miss'
- Cache key changed
- Or cache expired (7 days sin access)

## Cost
- Public repos: unlimited free
- Private: 2000 min/month free (Free plan), 3000 (Team), 50000 (Enterprise)
- Beyond: pay per minute

## Best practices
- **Fail fast** — matrix con `fail-fast: true` (default)
- **Small jobs** parallel para speed
- **Cache dependencies**
- **Pin action versions** (`@v4`, not `@main`)
- **Least privilege secrets**
- **Audit workflow runs** — quién triggered qué

title: GitLab CI: pipelines eficientes
body:
## `.gitlab-ci.yml` basics
```yaml
stages:
  - build
  - test
  - deploy

variables:
  DOCKER_DRIVER: overlay2

build:
  stage: build
  image: node:20
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npm run build
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - dist/
    expire_in: 1 hour

test:
  stage: test
  image: node:20
  script:
    - npm test
  coverage: '/Coverage: \d+.\d+%/'

deploy_prod:
  stage: deploy
  image: alpine:latest
  before_script:
    - apk add curl
  script:
    - ./deploy.sh production
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://myapp.com
  only:
    - main
  when: manual
```

## Runners
### Shared runners
GitLab.com hosted. Free minutes.

### Self-hosted runners
Instalar en tu infrastructure:
- Docker executor (recomendado)
- Shell executor
- Kubernetes executor (para escalabilidad)

### Register
```bash
gitlab-runner register
# Interactive: URL, token, name, executor
```

### Config file
`/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml`:
```toml
[[runners]]
  name = 'docker-runner'
  url = 'https://gitlab.com'
  token = '...'
  executor = 'docker'
  [runners.docker]
    image = 'alpine:latest'
    privileged = false
    volumes = ['/cache']
```

## Rules (moderno)
Más flexible que `only/except`:
```yaml
deploy:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == 'main'
      when: manual
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /^v/
      when: on_success
    - when: never
```

## Cache
```yaml
cache:
  key: ${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}
  paths:
    - node_modules/
    - .npm/
```

## Artifacts vs Cache
- **Artifacts** — passed to next stage, retained after pipeline
- **Cache** — reused across pipelines, per branch

## Include
```yaml
include:
  - template: Security/SAST.gitlab-ci.yml
  - local: .gitlab/ci/deploy.yml
  - remote: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/example/config.yml'
```

Reuse templates.

## Parent-child pipelines
Split large pipelines:
```yaml
trigger_child:
  trigger:
    include: child-pipeline.yml
    strategy: depend  # wait for child completion
```

## DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph)
Jobs run parallel where possible:
```yaml
deploy_frontend:
  needs: [build_frontend]

deploy_backend:
  needs: [build_backend, integration_tests]
```

Sin `needs`, jobs corren en stages secuenciales.

## Environments
```yaml
environments:
  - name: staging
    url: https://staging.myapp.com
    on_stop: stop_staging
```

GitLab UI shows environment status.

## Auto DevOps
GitLab feature: auto-build, test, deploy con zero config si sigue conventions.

Habilitá en project settings. Bueno para prototypes.

## Common issues
### 'Runner not picking up jobs'
- Runner offline
- Tags don't match
- Config wrong (`config.toml`)

### 'Docker permission denied'
- Runner user not in `docker` group
- Or use Kubernetes executor

### 'Cache not restored'
- Key wrong
- Cache stored en local runner (not shared)
- Use distributed cache (S3, MinIO)

### 'Pipeline stuck en pending'
- No shared runners available
- Self-hosted overloaded
- Check runner logs

## Security
### Protected variables
Only available en protected branches/tags.

### Masked variables
Hide sensitive values en logs.

### CI/CD tokens
Project/group access tokens en vez de personal tokens.

## Best practices
- **Small stages** — parallel para speed
- **Reuse templates** con includes
- **Cache aggressively** — nodemodules, pip cache
- **Protected environments** para prod
- **Manual gate** antes de prod deploy
- **Audit logs** — quién triggered qué

title: ArgoCD: GitOps deployment para Kubernetes
excerpt: Deploy K8s apps declaratively via Git.
body:
## GitOps concept
- Git = single source of truth
- Desired state en Git
- Auto-sync a K8s
- Drift detection + auto-heal

## ArgoCD
GitOps controller para Kubernetes.

## Install
```bash
kubectl create namespace argocd
kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml
```

### Access UI
```bash
kubectl port-forward svc/argocd-server -n argocd 8080:443
```
Browse to `https://localhost:8080`.

Initial password:
```bash
kubectl -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d
```

## CLI
```bash
brew install argocd
argocd login localhost:8080
```

## Create Application

### Declarative (recomendado)
```yaml
# applications/my-app.yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
    name: my-app
    namespace: argocd
spec:
    project: default
    source:
        repoURL: https://github.com/empresa/k8s-manifests
        targetRevision: main
        path: apps/my-app
    destination:
        server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
        namespace: production
    syncPolicy:
        automated:
            prune: true
            selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
            - CreateNamespace=true
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f applications/my-app.yaml
```

### Via CLI
```bash
argocd app create my-app \
    --repo https://github.com/empresa/k8s-manifests \
    --path apps/my-app \
    --dest-server https://kubernetes.default.svc \
    --dest-namespace production
```

## Repo structure
```
k8s-manifests/
  apps/
    my-app/
      deployment.yaml
      service.yaml
      ingress.yaml
      configmap.yaml
```

## Kustomize
Overlays por entorno:
```
k8s-manifests/
  base/
    deployment.yaml
    kustomization.yaml
  overlays/
    dev/
      kustomization.yaml
      patches.yaml
    prod/
      kustomization.yaml
      patches.yaml
```

ArgoCD detecta Kustomize automatically.

## Helm
```yaml
source:
    repoURL: https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
    targetRevision: 15.0.0
    chart: postgresql
    helm:
        values: |
            auth:
                postgresPassword: changeme
```

## Sync policies

### Manual
App shows 'OutOfSync' → click Sync.

### Auto
```yaml
syncPolicy:
    automated:
        prune: true      # delete removed resources
        selfHeal: true   # revert manual changes en cluster
```

## Multi-cluster
```bash
argocd cluster add my-cluster-context
```

One ArgoCD → multiple clusters.

### App Sets (múltiples apps de un template)
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
spec:
    generators:
      - list:
          elements:
            - env: dev
              cluster: dev-cluster
            - env: prod
              cluster: prod-cluster
    template:
        metadata:
            name: 'my-app-{{env}}'
        spec:
            source:
                path: 'overlays/{{env}}'
```

Genera 1 App per env.

## RBAC
### Users
Built-in local users o SSO (SAML, OIDC).

### Roles
```csv
p, role:developer, applications, get, */*, allow
p, role:developer, applications, sync, dev-*/*, allow
g, developer-group, role:developer
```

Developers pueden sync solo dev apps.

## Notifications
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
    name: argocd-notifications-cm
data:
    trigger.on-sync-succeeded: |
        - send: [slack]
    template.app-deployed: |
        message: 'App {{.app.metadata.name}} deployed'
```

Alerts a Slack/Teams/webhook.

## Rollback
ArgoCD UI → App → **History** → seleccionar revisión anterior → **Rollback**.

Or:
```bash
argocd app rollback my-app <revision-id>
```

## Secrets
Environment secrets no directly en Git. Use:
- **External Secrets Operator** (fetches from vault)
- **Sealed Secrets** (encrypted en Git)
- **SOPS** (Mozilla)

## Common issues

### 'App stuck en syncing'
- CRD not installed
- Namespace not exists
- Resource quota exceeded

### 'Out of sync but no changes'
- Somebody modified cluster manually
- `syncPolicy.selfHeal: true` will revert

### 'Auth issues con Git'
- SSH key permission
- Token expired
- Verify credentials en ArgoCD settings

## Best practices
- **1 repo por app** o mono-repo con clara separation
- **Environment overlays** (Kustomize o Helm values)
- **Automated sync + self-heal** para dev/staging
- **Manual approval** para prod (sync policy sin automated para prod app)
- **RBAC strict** — separate dev/ops permissions
- **Notifications** para deploys visibles

title: Terraform: modules + state management
excerpt: Estructurar Terraform con modules reutilizables + backend remoto.
body:
## Terraform basics
IaC declarativo. Provider → resource.

## Module structure
```
modules/
  vpc/
    main.tf
    variables.tf
    outputs.tf
    README.md
  ec2/
    main.tf
    variables.tf
    outputs.tf
environments/
  dev/
    main.tf
    backend.tf
    terraform.tfvars
  prod/
    main.tf
    backend.tf
    terraform.tfvars
```

## Module (VPC ejemplo)

### `modules/vpc/main.tf`
```hcl
resource 'aws_vpc' 'this' {
    cidr_block = var.cidr_block
    tags = merge({ Name = var.name }, var.tags)
}

resource 'aws_subnet' 'public' {
    count = length(var.public_subnets)
    vpc_id = aws_vpc.this.id
    cidr_block = var.public_subnets[count.index]
    availability_zone = var.availability_zones[count.index]
}
```

### `modules/vpc/variables.tf`
```hcl
variable 'name' { type = string }
variable 'cidr_block' { type = string }
variable 'public_subnets' { type = list(string) }
variable 'availability_zones' { type = list(string) }
variable 'tags' { type = map(string); default = {} }
```

### `modules/vpc/outputs.tf`
```hcl
output 'vpc_id' { value = aws_vpc.this.id }
output 'public_subnet_ids' { value = aws_subnet.public[*].id }
```

## Consume module
### `environments/prod/main.tf`
```hcl
module 'vpc' {
    source = '../../modules/vpc'
    name = 'prod-vpc'
    cidr_block = '10.0.0.0/16'
    public_subnets = ['10.0.1.0/24', '10.0.2.0/24']
    availability_zones = ['us-east-1a', 'us-east-1b']
    tags = { Environment = 'prod', Team = 'platform' }
}

output 'vpc_id' { value = module.vpc.vpc_id }
```

## Backend remoto (state en cloud)

### S3 (AWS)
```hcl
terraform {
    backend 's3' {
        bucket = 'my-terraform-state-prod'
        key = 'prod/terraform.tfstate'
        region = 'us-east-1'
        dynamodb_table = 'terraform-locks'    # locking
        encrypt = true
    }
}
```

### Azure Blob
```hcl
backend 'azurerm' {
    resource_group_name = 'terraform-state-rg'
    storage_account_name = 'tfstate'
    container_name = 'tfstate'
    key = 'prod.tfstate'
}
```

### GCS
```hcl
backend 'gcs' {
    bucket = 'my-tf-state'
    prefix = 'prod'
}
```

### Terraform Cloud (managed)
```hcl
terraform {
    cloud {
        organization = 'my-org'
        workspaces { name = 'prod' }
    }
}
```

## Workspaces
Multiple environments con mismo code:
```bash
terraform workspace new dev
terraform workspace new prod
terraform workspace select prod
```

Cada workspace = separate state.

## Commands
```bash
terraform init                # download providers, config backend
terraform plan                # preview changes
terraform apply               # apply
terraform destroy             # destroy resources
terraform state list          # ver resources tracked
terraform state show <resource>
terraform import <resource> <id>   # import existing to state
terraform fmt                 # format code
terraform validate            # syntax check
```

## Locking
Evita concurrent modifications:
- **S3 + DynamoDB** — recomendado
- **Terraform Cloud** — built-in

Si 2 devs corren `terraform apply` simultáneo:
- 1er locks state
- 2do espera (o fails)

## Sensitive values
```hcl
variable 'db_password' {
    type = string
    sensitive = true
}
```

Not printed en outputs.

### Best: source from vault
```hcl
data 'aws_secretsmanager_secret_version' 'db' {
    secret_id = 'db-creds'
}

locals {
    db_password = jsondecode(data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db.secret_string).password
}
```

## Refactoring
### Moving resources (avoid recreation)
```bash
terraform state mv aws_instance.web module.ec2.aws_instance.web
```

### Import existing
```bash
terraform import aws_instance.web i-abc123
```

Now Terraform manages ese existing resource.

## CI/CD
### GitHub Actions
```yaml
- uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
- run: terraform init
- run: terraform plan -out=tfplan
- run: terraform apply tfplan
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
```

### Best practice: separate plan and apply
- PR: plan (review changes)
- Merge: apply automatic

## Common issues

### 'State conflicts'
- Manual changes en cloud (drift)
- `terraform refresh` sync state
- Or import missing resources

### 'Provider version conflicts'
- Pin versions:
```hcl
terraform {
    required_providers {
        aws = { source = 'hashicorp/aws'; version = '~> 5.0' }
    }
}
```

### 'Slow plans'
- Refresh takes long con many resources
- `-refresh=false` skip (careful, may miss drift)

### 'Cannot destroy'
- Resource has dependent resources
- Manual cleanup en cloud first

## Best practices
- **Modules reusables** — no copy-paste
- **Backend remoto** siempre
- **State locking** obligatorio
- **Small state files** — split por servicio
- **Version providers** — no float latest
- **Plan antes de apply** — review con equipo
- **Sensitive marked** — no leak secrets

title: Ansible: playbooks + inventory best practices
body:
## Directory layout recomendada
```
ansible/
  ansible.cfg
  inventories/
    dev/
      hosts.yml
      group_vars/
        all.yml
        webservers.yml
      host_vars/
        web01.yml
    prod/
      hosts.yml
      group_vars/
      host_vars/
  roles/
    common/
    webserver/
    database/
  playbooks/
    site.yml
    webservers.yml
    dbservers.yml
  requirements.yml
```

## ansible.cfg
```ini
[defaults]
inventory = ./inventories/dev/hosts.yml
roles_path = ./roles
host_key_checking = False
retry_files_enabled = False
callback_whitelist = timer,profile_tasks
gathering = smart
fact_caching = jsonfile
fact_caching_connection = /tmp/ansible_facts

[ssh_connection]
pipelining = True
control_path = /tmp/ansible-ssh-%%h-%%p-%%r
```

## Inventory YAML
```yaml
# inventories/prod/hosts.yml
all:
  children:
    webservers:
      hosts:
        web01.empresa.local:
        web02.empresa.local:
      vars:
        http_port: 80
    dbservers:
      hosts:
        db01.empresa.local:
    lb:
      hosts:
        lb01.empresa.local:
```

## group_vars y host_vars

### `group_vars/all.yml`
Variables comunes:
```yaml
corporate_domain: empresa.local
syslog_server: syslog.empresa.local
```

### `group_vars/webservers.yml`
Specific to webservers group:
```yaml
httpd_service: apache2
httpd_port: 8080
```

### `host_vars/web01.empresa.local.yml`
Host-specific:
```yaml
httpd_port: 8081   # override group var
ssl_cert: /etc/ssl/web01.crt
```

## Roles

### Structure
```
roles/webserver/
  tasks/
    main.yml
  handlers/
    main.yml
  templates/
    httpd.conf.j2
  files/
    security.conf
  vars/
    main.yml
  defaults/
    main.yml
  meta/
    main.yml
  README.md
```

### `tasks/main.yml`
```yaml
- name: Install httpd
  package:
    name: '{{ httpd_service }}'
    state: present

- name: Deploy config
  template:
    src: httpd.conf.j2
    dest: /etc/httpd/httpd.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0644'
  notify: restart httpd

- name: Enable + start service
  systemd:
    name: '{{ httpd_service }}'
    enabled: true
    state: started
```

### `handlers/main.yml`
```yaml
- name: restart httpd
  systemd:
    name: '{{ httpd_service }}'
    state: restarted
```

Handlers only run if notified. Deduplicated (multiple notifies = 1 restart al final).

## Playbook
```yaml
---
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  roles:
    - common
    - webserver
  tasks:
    - name: Custom task after roles
      debug:
        msg: 'Webserver configured'
```

## Run
```bash
ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod/hosts.yml playbooks/webservers.yml

# Solo un host
ansible-playbook -i ... webservers.yml --limit web01.empresa.local

# Dry-run
ansible-playbook -i ... webservers.yml --check --diff

# Con tags
ansible-playbook -i ... webservers.yml --tags 'config'
```

## Vault (secrets)
### Encrypt file
```bash
ansible-vault encrypt group_vars/prod/secrets.yml
```

### Edit
```bash
ansible-vault edit group_vars/prod/secrets.yml
```

### Run playbook
```bash
ansible-playbook -i ... site.yml --ask-vault-pass
# O:
ansible-playbook -i ... site.yml --vault-password-file ~/.vault_pass
```

## Idempotency
Ansible tasks debe ser idempotent:
- Correr 2x = same result
- No side effects extras

Built-in modules ya son idempotent. Custom shell commands NO por default:
```yaml
- shell: cp file.txt /dest/    # ⚠ no idempotent

- copy: src=file.txt dest=/dest/    # ✓ idempotent
```

## Ansible collections
Modern packaging:
```yaml
# requirements.yml
collections:
  - community.general
  - amazon.aws
  - kubernetes.core
```

```bash
ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml
```

## Dynamic inventory
AWS EC2 auto-discovery:
```yaml
# inventories/aws_ec2.yml
plugin: amazon.aws.aws_ec2
regions:
  - us-east-1
keyed_groups:
  - key: tags.Environment
    prefix: env
```

```bash
ansible-inventory -i aws_ec2.yml --graph
```

## CI/CD integration
### GitHub Actions
```yaml
- run: pip install ansible
- run: ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod/hosts.yml site.yml
  env:
    ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE: /tmp/vault_pass
```

## AWX / Ansible Tower / Automation Platform
Web UI + centralized management:
- Job templates
- Scheduling
- RBAC
- Approval workflows
- Notifications

Enterprise deployments.

## Common issues

### 'sudo failed'
```yaml
- become: true
  become_method: sudo
  # or: doas, su, pfexec
```

### 'Host key verification failed'
First connect:
```bash
ssh-keyscan host >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
```

Or disable en `ansible.cfg`.

### 'Slow'
Pipelining:
```ini
[ssh_connection]
pipelining = True
```

Speedup 3-4x.

### 'Facts gathering slow'
```yaml
- hosts: all
  gather_facts: false   # skip if not needed
```

Or cache facts.

## Best practices
- **Roles reusables** — no copiar tasks
- **Vault** para secrets
- **--check --diff** antes de real run
- **Small playbooks** — single responsibility
- **Documentation** en README de cada role
- **CI validation** — ansible-lint, yamllint
- **Tagging** — para running subsets

title: HashiCorp Vault: secrets management
excerpt: Almacenamiento centralizado de secrets con Vault.
body:
## Vault
Secrets management enterprise:
- Store passwords, API keys, certs
- Dynamic secrets (short-lived, auto-generated)
- Encryption as a service
- Audit logging
- Multi-provider support

## Install
### Dev mode (local testing)
```bash
vault server -dev
# Auto-unsealed, root token en console
```

### Production
- Deploy en HA con Consul or integrated storage
- 3-5 nodes (Raft consensus)

### Docker
```bash
docker run -d --cap-add=IPC_LOCK \
    -e VAULT_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID=root \
    -p 8200:8200 \
    vault
```

## Access
### UI
`http://vault:8200/ui`

### CLI
```bash
export VAULT_ADDR='http://vault:8200'
vault login root
```

### API
HTTPS REST endpoints.

## Secrets engines

### KV (key-value)
Store arbitrary secrets:
```bash
vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2

vault kv put secret/prod/db password=secret123 username=admin
vault kv get secret/prod/db
```

### PKI (certificates)
Genera certs dynamically:
```bash
vault secrets enable pki
vault write pki/root/generate/internal common_name='empresa.local'
vault write pki/roles/web allowed_domains='empresa.local' allow_subdomains=true

vault write pki/issue/web common_name='api.empresa.local'
# Returns cert + key + chain
```

### Database (dynamic creds)
```bash
vault secrets enable database
vault write database/config/postgres \
    plugin_name=postgresql-database-plugin \
    connection_url='postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@localhost:5432/mydb' \
    username='vault' \
    password='vault-pass'

vault write database/roles/readonly \
    db_name=postgres \
    creation_statements='CREATE ROLE "{{name}}" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD ...' \
    default_ttl='1h' \
    max_ttl='24h'

vault read database/creds/readonly
# Returns temp user + password, expires 1h
```

App cada request obtiene fresh creds.

### AWS
```bash
vault secrets enable aws
vault write aws/config/root \
    access_key=... secret_key=...
vault write aws/roles/deploy \
    credential_type=iam_user \
    policy_arns='arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess'

vault read aws/creds/deploy
# Temporary AWS credentials
```

### Transit (encryption as a service)
```bash
vault secrets enable transit
vault write -f transit/keys/my-key

vault write transit/encrypt/my-key plaintext=$(echo 'sensitive' | base64)
# Returns ciphertext:vault:v1:xxxxxxxx

vault write transit/decrypt/my-key ciphertext=vault:v1:xxx
```

Apps envían plaintext, get ciphertext. Vault holds the key.

## Auth methods

### AppRole (M2M)
Apps con role_id + secret_id:
```bash
vault auth enable approle
vault write auth/approle/role/my-app policies='readonly' token_ttl=1h
vault read auth/approle/role/my-app/role-id
vault write -f auth/approle/role/my-app/secret-id
```

App uses role_id + secret_id → token.

### Kubernetes
Pods auto-authenticate con SA tokens:
```bash
vault auth enable kubernetes
vault write auth/kubernetes/config \
    kubernetes_host='https://k8s.local' \
    kubernetes_ca_cert=@/path/ca.crt
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/my-app \
    bound_service_account_names=my-app \
    bound_service_account_namespaces=production \
    policies=readonly
```

Pod service account = Vault identity.

### LDAP / OIDC
Enterprise SSO integration.

## Policies
HCL syntax:
```hcl
# Path 'secret/prod/*'
path 'secret/data/prod/*' {
    capabilities = ['read', 'list']
}

path 'secret/data/dev/*' {
    capabilities = ['create', 'read', 'update', 'delete', 'list']
}

# Deny production changes
path 'secret/data/prod/database' {
    capabilities = ['deny']
}
```

Write policy:
```bash
vault policy write my-policy policy.hcl
```

Assign to role o user.

## Uso desde apps

### Node.js
```javascript
const vault = require('node-vault')({
    endpoint: 'https://vault.empresa.local:8200',
    token: process.env.VAULT_TOKEN
});

const secret = await vault.read('secret/data/prod/db');
console.log(secret.data.data.password);
```

### Python
```python
import hvac
client = hvac.Client(url='https://vault:8200', token=token)
secret = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(path='prod/db')
print(secret['data']['data']['password'])
```

### CI/CD
GitHub Actions:
```yaml
- uses: hashicorp/vault-action@v3
  with:
    url: https://vault.empresa.local:8200
    method: approle
    roleId: ${{ secrets.VAULT_ROLE_ID }}
    secretId: ${{ secrets.VAULT_SECRET_ID }}
    secrets: |
        secret/data/prod/db password | DB_PASS
```

## Unsealing (production)
Vault starts sealed. Requires unseal keys:
```bash
vault operator unseal <key1>
vault operator unseal <key2>
vault operator unseal <key3>
```

Shamir's: 3 of 5 keys needed. Distribute to different people.

Auto-unseal con cloud KMS más operational (no manual step).

## Audit
```bash
vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault_audit.log
```

All operations logged. Send to SIEM.

## HA
### Integrated Storage (Raft)
Recommended:
```hcl
storage 'raft' {
    path = '/vault/data'
    node_id = 'node1'
}
cluster_addr = 'https://node1:8201'
api_addr = 'https://node1:8200'
```

3-5 nodes. Automatic leader election.

### Consul (legacy)
Alternative, más complex.

## Common issues

### 'Vault sealed'
After restart. Manual unseal or auto-unseal.

### 'Permission denied'
Token lacks policy. Check policies assigned.

### 'Token expired'
Renew before expiration o obtain new.

### 'Slow perf'
- Storage backend bottleneck (Consul, disk)
- Too many audit backends
- Certificate rotations frequent

## Best practices
- **Never store static secrets long-term** — use dynamic
- **Rotate keys** regularly
- **Audit** everything
- **Least privilege** policies
- **HA setup** obligatorio
- **Backup regularly** (raft snapshots)
- **DR drill** — practice restore
- **Cert rotation** automated

title: Prometheus + Grafana: monitoring stack
excerpt: Setup stack de monitoring open source.
body:
## Prometheus
Metrics collection + storage + querying.

## Install (Docker)
```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3'
services:
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
    ports:
      - '9090:9090'
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'
    environment:
      GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: admin
```

## Prometheus config
`prometheus.yml`:
```yaml
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'node'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['node-exporter:9100']

  - job_name: 'kubernetes-pods'
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
    relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape]
        action: keep
        regex: true

  - job_name: 'app'
    metrics_path: '/metrics'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['app:8080']
```

## Exporters
Standard components exposen metrics format Prometheus:

- **node_exporter** — OS metrics (CPU, RAM, disk)
- **cadvisor** — container metrics
- **kube-state-metrics** — Kubernetes objects state
- **postgres_exporter** — PostgreSQL
- **redis_exporter** — Redis
- **blackbox_exporter** — HTTP/TCP probes
- **snmp_exporter** — SNMP devices

### Instrument custom app

#### Python
```python
from prometheus_client import Counter, Histogram, start_http_server

requests = Counter('app_requests_total', 'Total requests', ['method', 'endpoint'])
latency = Histogram('app_latency_seconds', 'Request latency')

@app.route('/api/data')
def data():
    requests.labels(method='GET', endpoint='/api/data').inc()
    with latency.time():
        # ... process ...
        return 'OK'

start_http_server(8000)   # metrics en /metrics
```

#### Node.js
```javascript
const promClient = require('prom-client');
const register = promClient.register;
promClient.collectDefaultMetrics();

const counter = new promClient.Counter({
    name: 'app_requests_total',
    help: 'Total requests',
    labelNames: ['method', 'endpoint']
});

app.get('/api/data', (req, res) => {
    counter.inc({ method: 'GET', endpoint: '/api/data' });
    res.send('OK');
});

app.get('/metrics', async (req, res) => {
    res.set('Content-Type', register.contentType);
    res.end(await register.metrics());
});
```

## PromQL
Query language.

### Ejemplos
```
# CPU usage per instance
rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode='user'}[5m])

# Memory available %
(node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes) * 100

# Request rate por endpoint
rate(app_requests_total[1m])

# 95th percentile latency
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(app_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))

# Errors per second
rate(app_requests_total{status='5xx'}[1m])
```

## Grafana

### Add Prometheus as data source
1. Grafana UI → **Data Sources → Add** → Prometheus
2. URL: `http://prometheus:9090`
3. Save + test

### Create dashboard
1. **+ Create → Dashboard**
2. Add Panel
3. Query (PromQL)
4. Visualization type (graph, gauge, table, stat)

### Popular dashboards (import ID)
- `1860` — Node Exporter Full
- `315` — Kubernetes cluster
- `9614` — nginx
- `9628` — postgres

Just import por ID desde Grafana marketplace.

### Alerting
**Alerting → Alert rules**:
```yaml
name: HighCPU
expr: rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode='user'}[5m]) > 0.8
for: 5m
annotations:
    summary: 'High CPU on {{$labels.instance}}'
```

Send to:
- Slack
- PagerDuty
- Email
- Webhook

## Alertmanager
Separate service para route alertas:
```yaml
# alertmanager.yml
route:
  receiver: 'slack'
  group_by: [alertname]
  routes:
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: pagerduty

receivers:
  - name: slack
    slack_configs:
      - webhook_url: 'https://hooks.slack.com/...'
        channel: '#alerts'
  - name: pagerduty
    pagerduty_configs:
      - service_key: 'xxx'
```

Prometheus → Alertmanager → notifications.

## Storage
Default: Prometheus stores 15 days local.

Long-term storage:
- **Thanos** — objecto storage (S3)
- **VictoriaMetrics** — alternative
- **Cortex** — multi-tenant

## HA
Dual Prometheus instances scraping same targets. Alertmanager cluster de-dups alerts.

## Common issues

### 'Target down'
- Firewall
- Service not exposing /metrics
- Wrong port

### 'Cardinality explosion'
- Labels con demasiados valores únicos (usernames, timestamps)
- Fix: label carefully, avoid high-cardinality dimensions

### 'Slow queries'
- Aggregate primero (recording rules)
- Reduce range
- Increase Prometheus resources

## Best practices
- **Instrument early** — app metrics desde el arranque
- **Naming convention** — `<domain>_<subject>_<action>_<unit>` (ej: `app_requests_total_count`)
- **Labels útiles** — env, service, version
- **Recording rules** para queries frequently used
- **Alerts actionable** — con runbook links
- **Dashboards por audience** — dev, ops, business

title: Kubernetes: Operators y CRDs custom
excerpt: Automatizar operaciones custom con Kubernetes Operators.
body:
## Operator pattern
Extend K8s con custom logic:
- **CRD** (Custom Resource Definition) — new resource type
- **Controller** — logic that reconciles CRD state

Operators automatan tareas complejas:
- Deploy + upgrade DBs (Postgres, MongoDB)
- Manage certificates (cert-manager)
- Backup schedules
- Service mesh policies

## CRD example: Postgres cluster

### CRD definition
```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: postgresclusters.database.example.com
spec:
  group: database.example.com
  names:
    kind: PostgresCluster
    plural: postgresclusters
    singular: postgrescluster
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                replicas: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 10 }
                version: { type: string }
                storage: { type: string }
```

### Instance
```yaml
apiVersion: database.example.com/v1
kind: PostgresCluster
metadata:
  name: my-db
spec:
  replicas: 3
  version: '16.0'
  storage: 100Gi
```

### Controller
Logic que watch CRD y crea underlying resources:
- StatefulSet
- PVCs
- Services
- ConfigMaps (config del Postgres)

Maneja upgrades, failover, backups automáticamente.

## Operator SDK
Build operators en Go/Python/Ansible:

### Install
```bash
brew install operator-sdk
```

### Create operator
```bash
operator-sdk init --domain=example.com --repo=github.com/example/my-operator
operator-sdk create api --group=database --version=v1 --kind=PostgresCluster --resource --controller
```

### Controller code (Go)
```go
func (r *PostgresClusterReconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, req ctrl.Request) (ctrl.Result, error) {
    var cluster databasev1.PostgresCluster
    if err := r.Get(ctx, req.NamespacedName, &cluster); err != nil {
        return ctrl.Result{}, client.IgnoreNotFound(err)
    }
    
    // Create StatefulSet
    // Create Services
    // Update status
    
    return ctrl.Result{Requeue: true, RequeueAfter: 30 * time.Second}, nil
}
```

## Popular operators

### Cert-manager
Automate TLS cert lifecycle (Let's Encrypt, corporate CA):
```yaml
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: my-tls
spec:
  secretName: my-tls-cert
  issuerRef:
    name: letsencrypt-prod
  dnsNames: [myapp.empresa.com]
```

Operator handles ACME flow, storage, renewal.

### Prometheus Operator
Deploy Prometheus + config as CRDs:
```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: Prometheus
metadata:
  name: my-prometheus
spec:
  replicas: 2
  serviceMonitorSelector: {}
```

### Kafka Operator (Strimzi)
Deploy + manage Kafka clusters.

### Postgres Operators
- **Zalando/postgres-operator**
- **CrunchyData PGO**
- **CloudNativePG**

### External Secrets Operator
Sync secrets from Vault/AWS/Azure to K8s Secrets.

## Install operator
### Via Helm
```bash
helm repo add jetstack https://charts.jetstack.io
helm install cert-manager jetstack/cert-manager --namespace cert-manager --create-namespace
```

### Via OLM (Operator Lifecycle Manager)
Manages operators declaratively.

### Manual manifests
```bash
kubectl apply -f https://operator-releases/latest/operator.yaml
```

## CRDs discovery
```bash
kubectl api-resources
kubectl get crds
kubectl explain postgrescluster.spec
```

## Debug controller
### Logs
```bash
kubectl logs -n operators-system deployment/my-operator-controller-manager -c manager
```

### Events
```bash
kubectl describe postgrescluster my-db
```

Check events section para reconciliation issues.

### Status field
Custom resources typically have `.status` section — read for state.

## Common issues

### 'CRD version mismatch'
- Update CRD → old resources maynot conform
- Use conversion webhooks

### 'Controller not reconciling'
- Check permissions (RBAC)
- Check controller deployment running
- Check RESOURCEwatches

### 'Cascade delete missing'
Set owner references:
```go
ctrl.SetControllerReference(&cluster, &statefulSet, r.Scheme)
```

Deleting parent → children auto-deleted.

## Best practices
- **Idempotent reconciliation** — safe to run repeatedly
- **Status updates** — record current state
- **Events** — user-facing history
- **Metrics** — Prometheus-instrument controller
- **RBAC minimal** — only what operator needs
- **Version CRDs** — evolve without breaking existing

## When NOT to write operator
Simpler alternatives:
- Helm chart
- kustomize
- Simple deployment

Operators worth el effort para:
- Complex state management (DBs, brokers)
- Custom domain logic
- Reusable across teams

title: SonarQube: code quality gates
tags: sonarqube, code quality, static analysis, ci
excerpt: Análisis estático de código para calidad + security.
body:
## SonarQube
Plataforma SaaS/self-hosted para:
- Static code analysis
- Bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells
- Coverage integration
- Quality gates (block bad code)
- Multi-language support

## Install (Docker)
```yaml
version: '3'
services:
  sonarqube:
    image: sonarqube:community
    ports:
      - '9000:9000'
    environment:
      SONAR_JDBC_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/sonar
      SONAR_JDBC_USERNAME: sonar
      SONAR_JDBC_PASSWORD: sonar
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: sonar
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: sonar
      POSTGRES_DB: sonar
```

Access: `http://localhost:9000` — default admin/admin.

## Scan un proyecto

### Local
```bash
sonar-scanner \
    -Dsonar.projectKey=my-app \
    -Dsonar.sources=. \
    -Dsonar.host.url=http://sonarqube:9000 \
    -Dsonar.token=my-token
```

### `sonar-project.properties`
```properties
sonar.projectKey=my-app
sonar.projectName=My App
sonar.projectVersion=1.0
sonar.sources=src
sonar.tests=test
sonar.language=javascript
sonar.exclusions=**/node_modules/**,**/dist/**
sonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths=coverage/lcov.info
```

## Language plugins
Install from marketplace:
- Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C#, Go, Rust
- 30+ languages

## CI integration

### GitHub Actions
```yaml
- name: SonarQube Scan
  uses: sonarsource/sonarqube-scan-action@master
  env:
    SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
    SONAR_HOST_URL: https://sonarqube.empresa.local
```

### Jenkins
```groovy
stage('SonarQube') {
    steps {
        withSonarQubeEnv('SonarQube') {
            sh 'mvn sonar:sonar'
        }
    }
}
stage('Quality Gate') {
    steps {
        waitForQualityGate abortPipeline: true
    }
}
```

Build fails si quality gate no pasa.

## Quality gates
Rules que definen 'good code':
- Code coverage > 80%
- 0 blocker bugs
- 0 critical vulnerabilities
- Duplicated code < 3%

**New code**: apply solo a código nuevo (last 30 days) para incremental improvement.

### Create gate
UI → **Quality Gates** → New:
- Condition: Coverage on new code > 80
- Condition: Bugs on new code = 0
- Etc.

Assign to project.

## Issues categorías

### Bugs
Coding errors:
- Null pointer
- Off-by-one
- Uncaught exceptions

### Vulnerabilities
Security issues:
- SQL injection
- XSS
- Hardcoded secrets
- Weak crypto

### Code smells
Maintenance issues:
- Duplicated code
- Long methods
- High complexity
- Unused imports

### Security hotspots
Manual review needed:
- Uses of eval()
- Weak randomness
- HTTP without TLS

## Coverage
SonarQube reads coverage from your test tool:
- JavaScript: LCOV
- Java: JaCoCo XML
- Python: coverage.py XML
- C#: OpenCover / dotCover

Configure `sonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths` etc.

## Custom rules
Extend SonarQube con custom rules (Java plugin development).

O use SonarLint IDE plugins para catch en dev time (before commit).

## Common issues

### 'Scanner cannot connect'
- Wrong URL
- Firewall
- Token invalid

### 'Coverage 0%'
- LCOV file not generated antes de scan
- Wrong path en config
- Tests actually running?

### 'False positives'
- Suppress con `//NOSONAR` inline
- Or in UI: mark as 'False Positive'

### 'Sonar out of memory'
Large repos:
```bash
SONAR_SCANNER_OPTS='-Xmx4G' sonar-scanner
```

## SonarCloud (SaaS)
Alternative sin self-host:
- Free para open source
- Paid para private repos
- Integrated con GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket

## Best practices
- **Quality gate en CI** — block merges de bad code
- **Focus en new code** — no re-litigate legacy
- **Weekly review** — ver metrics trend
- **Assign issues** — accountability
- **Suppress con justification** — no ignorar silently
- **Regular exports** — audit trail

title: Docker BuildKit + multi-arch builds
body:
## BuildKit
Modern builder de Docker:
- Parallel builds
- Better caching
- Multi-arch nativo
- Secrets injection sin capa

## Enable
```bash
export DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1
docker build -t myapp .
```

O en Docker daemon config:
```json
{ 'features': { 'buildkit': true } }
```

## Multi-stage con BuildKit
Más eficiente — solo stages needed son built:
```dockerfile
FROM node:20 AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM nginx:alpine AS runtime
COPY --from=builder /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
```

## Cache mounts
Persistent cache entre builds:
```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.4
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm \
    npm ci
```

npm cache persist across builds — mucho más fast.

## Secret injection
Sin comprometer capa:
```bash
docker build --secret id=aws,src=$HOME/.aws/credentials -t myapp .
```

```dockerfile
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=aws \
    aws s3 cp s3://bucket/file .
```

Secret NO persiste en image.

## SSH mounts
Build con private repos:
```bash
docker build --ssh default -t myapp .
```

```dockerfile
RUN --mount=type=ssh git clone git@github.com:private/repo.git
```

## Multi-arch builds (buildx)

### Setup
```bash
docker buildx create --name multi --use
docker buildx inspect --bootstrap
```

### Build para múltiples arquitecturas
```bash
docker buildx build \
    --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/arm/v7 \
    -t myregistry/myapp:latest \
    --push \
    .
```

Pushed manifest lists — clients auto-select correct arch.

### Local test
```bash
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 --load -t myapp:arm64 .
docker run --platform linux/arm64 myapp:arm64
```

QEMU emulation.

## Use cases
- Servers ARM64 (AWS Graviton, Ampere)
- Apple M1/M2/M3 development
- Raspberry Pi
- Cost savings (ARM often cheaper en cloud)

## Caching strategies

### Layer caching (default)
Same layer contents = cache hit.

### Registry cache
```bash
docker buildx build \
    --cache-from type=registry,ref=myregistry/myapp:cache \
    --cache-to type=registry,ref=myregistry/myapp:cache,mode=max \
    -t myregistry/myapp:latest .
```

Shared cache entre CI runs.

### GitHub Actions cache
```yaml
- uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
  with:
    context: .
    push: true
    tags: myapp:latest
    cache-from: type=gha
    cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
```

## Build performance tips

### 1. Order Dockerfile efficiently
Put fastest-changing content last:
```dockerfile
COPY package.json ./       # 1: rarely changes
RUN npm ci                 # 2: benefits from #1 cache
COPY . .                   # 3: changes often
RUN npm run build
```

### 2. Use .dockerignore
```
node_modules
.git
*.log
.env
dist
```

Smaller context = faster.

### 3. Multi-stage
Builder tools no need to be en final image.

### 4. Minimize layers
Combine RUN:
```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

vs 3 separate RUNs.

## BuildKit-specific features

### Conditional stages
```dockerfile
ARG TARGET=production
FROM base AS production
RUN production-only-setup

FROM base AS development
RUN dev-tools-install

FROM ${TARGET} AS final
```

Build with `--build-arg TARGET=development`.

### Heredocs (BuildKit 1.4+)
```dockerfile
RUN <<EOF
apt-get update
apt-get install -y curl
rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
EOF
```

Cleaner than && chains.

## Debug builds
### Verbose
```bash
docker buildx build --progress plain .
```

See every command output.

### Interactive
```bash
docker buildx build --target builder -t debug .
docker run -it debug sh
```

Inspect intermediate stage.

## Common issues

### 'exec format error'
Running ARM binary on AMD or vice versa. Check target platform.

### 'Multi-arch push fails'
- Registry doesn't support manifest lists (rare)
- Docker Hub y major registries OK

### 'Build slow'
- No cache (first build)
- Enable BuildKit
- Use cache mounts

### 'Secret leaked en image'
- Don't ADD .env files
- Use --mount=type=secret
- Never COPY credentials

## Best practices
- **BuildKit always** — no reason to disable
- **Multi-stage** — smaller runtime images
- **Multi-arch** para portability
- **Cache** aggressively — CI y local
- **.dockerignore** curated
- **Scan images** después build (Trivy, Snyk)

title: Kubernetes StatefulSet: bases de datos + apps stateful
excerpt: Deploy DBs y apps con estado en K8s con StatefulSets.
body:
## StatefulSet
Controlador K8s para apps stateful:
- Ordered deployment (pod-0, pod-1, pod-2)
- Stable network identity (DNS predecible)
- Persistent storage per pod
- Ordered scaling + rolling updates

## Vs Deployment
- **Deployment**: stateless (web apps) — pods interchangeable
- **StatefulSet**: stateful — cada pod tiene identidad única

## Example: PostgreSQL primary + replicas
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: postgres
spec:
  serviceName: postgres
  replicas: 3
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: postgres } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: postgres } }
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:16
          ports: [{ containerPort: 5432, name: postgres }]
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: { name: postgres, key: password }
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata: { name: data }
      spec:
        accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
        storageClassName: fast-ssd
        resources:
          requests: { storage: 100Gi }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres
spec:
  clusterIP: None    # Headless service — required por StatefulSet
  selector: { app: postgres }
  ports:
    - port: 5432
      targetPort: 5432
```

## Pod naming
StatefulSet nombra pods predictibly:
- `postgres-0`
- `postgres-1`
- `postgres-2`

## DNS names
Each pod has stable DNS:
- `postgres-0.postgres.default.svc.cluster.local`
- `postgres-1.postgres.default.svc.cluster.local`

Apps referencia por hostname específico (útil para primary/replica setup).

## Storage
`volumeClaimTemplates` genera PVC por pod:
- `data-postgres-0` → PV 100Gi
- `data-postgres-1` → PV 100Gi
- `data-postgres-2` → PV 100Gi

Delete pod → PVC persist. Pod recreated → same PVC reattached.

Delete StatefulSet: PVCs NO se eliminan (default). Preserva datos.

## Scaling
```bash
kubectl scale statefulset postgres --replicas=5
```

Pods created en orden: postgres-3, postgres-4.

### Scale down
```bash
kubectl scale statefulset postgres --replicas=1
```

Pods removed en reverse: postgres-2, postgres-1. Data (PVC) preserved.

## Rolling update
```bash
kubectl set image statefulset postgres postgres=postgres:16.1
```

Pods updated en reverse order: postgres-2 primero, luego 1, 0.

### Partition update
```yaml
spec:
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 2
```

Solo pods con ordinal >= 2 updated. Canary release.

## Init pod
Custom init logic:
```yaml
initContainers:
    - name: init
      image: postgres:16
      command: ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'setup_replication.sh']
```

Runs once at pod start, before main containers.

## Anti-affinity (spread across nodes)
```yaml
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels: { app: postgres }
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

Cada pod en distinct node. Improve HA.

## Backups
StatefulSets don't handle backups automatically.

### Options
- Cron job que dumps DB → object storage
- Volume snapshots (CSI driver)
- Operator-managed (CloudNativePG, etc.)

### Volume snapshot
```yaml
apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: VolumeSnapshot
metadata:
  name: postgres-snapshot-2026-07-28
spec:
  volumeSnapshotClassName: csi-snapclass
  source:
    persistentVolumeClaimName: data-postgres-0
```

## Debugging
### Ver pods
```bash
kubectl get pods -l app=postgres
kubectl describe pod postgres-0
kubectl logs postgres-0
```

### Exec into pod
```bash
kubectl exec -it postgres-0 -- bash
```

### Check volume mount
```bash
kubectl exec postgres-0 -- df -h /var/lib/postgresql/data
```

## Common issues

### 'PVC pending'
- StorageClass no exists
- No provisioner
- Insufficient PV pool

### 'Pod stuck en Init'
- Init container failing
- Config wrong (env vars, secrets)

### 'Data lost after pod restart'
- Volume no mounted correctly
- Wrong path en mountPath
- PVC deleted accidentally

### 'DNS resolution failing'
- Headless service missing
- CoreDNS issue

## Best practices
- **Headless service** (`clusterIP: None`) obligatorio
- **Anti-affinity** across nodes
- **Persistent storage** con backup strategy
- **Resource limits** — cada pod DB is heavy
- **Monitoring** integrated (Prometheus)
- **DR plan** documented
- **Consider Operators** para complex apps (Postgres, Kafka, Mongo)

title: GitHub Copilot / Cursor: AI-assisted development
excerpt: Uso efectivo de AI coding assistants.
body:
## Herramientas actuales
- **GitHub Copilot** — Microsoft, integrated con VS Code
- **Cursor** — full IDE based on VS Code
- **Claude Code** — Anthropic CLI
- **Codeium** — free alternative
- **Amazon Q Developer** — AWS ecosystem

## Setup GitHub Copilot

### Subscribe
github.com/features/copilot → suscripción individual o business ($10-19/mo).

### Install extension
VS Code marketplace → 'GitHub Copilot'.

### Login
Command palette → 'GitHub Copilot: Sign In'.

## Basic usage

### Inline suggestions
Start typing → grey ghost text sugerencia:
- **Tab** — accept
- **Esc** — reject
- **Alt+]** o **Alt+[** — cycle alternatives

### Comment-driven
```python
# Function to parse CSV file and return list of dicts
def parse_csv(...):
    # Copilot fills in
```

### Multi-line generation
Start empty function → Copilot completes.

## Copilot Chat
Sidebar chat, ask questions about code:
- 'Explain this function'
- 'Refactor this to use async'
- 'Add error handling'
- 'Write tests for this'

### Slash commands
- `/explain` — explain selected code
- `/fix` — suggest fix
- `/tests` — generate tests
- `/doc` — add documentation

### Refer files
`@workspace` — search entire codebase
`@vscode` — VS Code-specific help
`#file:app.py` — reference specific file

## Cursor específico

### Ctrl+K
Inline edit — describe cambio, applies:
- 'Convert this to async'
- 'Add error handling'
- 'Extract to function'

### Cmd+L (Chat)
Sidebar chat como Copilot Chat.

### @-mentions
`@Codebase` — search project
`@Web` — search internet
`@Docs` — reference docs

### Composer
Multi-file editing con AI:
- 'Add authentication to app.py y routes.py'
- AI edita ambos coherently

## Productivity patterns

### 1. Boilerplate
Routine code:
```typescript
interface User {
    id: string;
    name: string;
    email: string;
    // Copilot completes: createdAt, updatedAt, etc.
}
```

### 2. Repetitive transformations
Once shown 2-3 examples, Copilot completes rest:
```javascript
const formatName = (u) => `${u.firstName} ${u.lastName}`;
const formatEmail = (u) => u.email.toLowerCase();
// Copilot suggests: formatPhone, formatAddress...
```

### 3. Test generation
Write function → Copilot writes tests.

### 4. Documentation
Write JSDoc comment start → Copilot completes.

### 5. API integrations
Describe endpoint → Copilot writes fetch/axios code.

## Cuando NO usar
- Code sensitive con business logic proprietary (Copilot may leak patterns)
- Compliance-strict code (some orgs prohibit)
- When you don't understand what it generates — dangerous en prod

## Best practices

### 1. Review carefully
AI hallucinations reales:
- Nombres de funciones inexistentes
- APIs incorrect
- Security anti-patterns

Always verify.

### 2. Test AI-generated code
Generated ≠ correct. Run tests. Actually execute.

### 3. Learn from suggestions
Don't blindly accept — understand:
- Why this pattern?
- Better alternatives?
- Edge cases missed?

### 4. Prompt engineering
Better comments = better suggestions:
```
# BAD: parse data

# GOOD: parse CSV with columns 'name', 'email', 'date' where date is ISO format.
# Return list of dicts with parsed date objects.
```

### 5. Use for specific tasks, not architecture
Good for:
- Boilerplate
- Well-defined algorithms
- Repetitive code

Bad for:
- Architecture decisions
- Business logic (may hallucinate rules)
- Performance tuning

## Security considerations

### Sensitive data
Copilot en Business/Enterprise plans no usa código para train models. Individual plan puede.

Check settings + org policy.

### License concerns
AI may generate code similar to training data (GitHub repos). Uncertain legal territory.

GitHub Copilot Enterprise includes IP indemnity.

### Code injection
AI could suggest exploitable code:
- Unsanitized inputs
- Hardcoded credentials
- SQL injection prone patterns

Security review necessary.

## Enterprise adoption

### Rollout plan
1. Pilot con 10-20 developers
2. Gather feedback
3. Metrics: productivity, code quality
4. Expand or adjust

### Policies
- What code can/cannot use AI
- Review requirements
- Training completed antes de use
- Security guidelines

### ROI
Studies:
- ~55% faster para common tasks
- Better satisfaction (dev-reported)
- Mixed impact en code quality (needs review discipline)

## Emerging patterns

### AI-first refactoring
'Convert this Python 2 app to Python 3' — AI handles bulk changes.

### Code review with AI
AI reviewer comments en PRs (GitHub Copilot for PR reviews).

### Debugging co-pilot
'This test fails with error X — why?'

AI analyzes context.

### Documentation gen
Input: undocumented codebase.
Output: complete docs.

## Future direction
- Better context awareness (full repos)
- Multi-file coherent edits
- Test + implementation together
- Deployment automation

AI coding assistants ya son productividad standard. Adopt or fall behind.

title: kubectl productivity: alias + plugins
excerpt: Speed-ups útiles para trabajar con kubectl día a día.
body:
## Aliases básicos
### `~/.bashrc` o `~/.zshrc`
```bash
alias k=kubectl
alias kg='kubectl get'
alias kd='kubectl describe'
alias kdel='kubectl delete'
alias kl='kubectl logs'
alias kex='kubectl exec -it'
alias kaf='kubectl apply -f'
alias kctx='kubectl config current-context'
```

## Autocomplete
```bash
source <(kubectl completion bash)   # o zsh
echo 'source <(kubectl completion bash)' >> ~/.bashrc

# Alias autocomplete
complete -F __start_kubectl k
```

Tab-completion para todos los comandos.

## Namespace shortcuts
```bash
k config set-context --current --namespace=production

# O con plugin kubens
kubens production
```

## kubectx (context switching)
```bash
brew install kubectx
```

```bash
kubectx prod        # switch to prod context
kubens app-team     # switch namespace
kubectx -           # switch to previous
```

## Plugins útiles (via krew)
### Install krew
```bash
cd $(mktemp -d) && \
    curl -fsSLO 'https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/krew/releases/latest/download/krew-linux_amd64.tar.gz' && \
    tar zxvf krew-linux_amd64.tar.gz && \
    ./krew-linux_amd64 install krew

export PATH=$HOME/.krew/bin:$PATH
```

### Popular plugins
```bash
kubectl krew install ns          # kubens alternative
kubectl krew install ctx         # kubectx alternative
kubectl krew install stern       # multi-pod logs
kubectl krew install neat        # cleanup YAML output
kubectl krew install tree        # hierarchy view
kubectl krew install score       # security analysis
kubectl krew install access-matrix   # RBAC visualization
kubectl krew install rakkess     # RBAC check
kubectl krew install view-secret # decode secrets
kubectl krew install debug-shell # debug utilities
```

## Comandos avanzados

### Get with output format
```bash
k get pods -o wide
k get pods -o json
k get pods -o yaml
k get pods -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase'
k get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
```

### Watch
```bash
k get pods -w    # continuous updates
```

### Filter
```bash
k get pods --field-selector status.phase=Running
k get pods --selector app=my-app
k get pods -A   # all namespaces
```

### Sort
```bash
k get pods --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp'
k top pods --sort-by=cpu
```

## Logs
### Follow
```bash
kl -f pod-name
```

### Multiple containers
```bash
kl -f pod-name -c container-name
kl -f pod-name --all-containers
```

### Since
```bash
kl --since=1h pod-name
kl --since-time='2026-07-28T10:00:00Z' pod-name
```

### Stern (multi-pod)
```bash
stern -n production app-name
```

Logs de múltiples pods, colored.

## Exec
### Interactive shell
```bash
kex pod-name -- bash
kex pod-name -- sh
```

### Single command
```bash
k exec pod-name -- env
k exec pod-name -- ls /app
```

### Debug ephemeral container
```bash
k debug -it pod-name --image=busybox --target=main-container
```

## Port forward
```bash
k port-forward pod/pod-name 8080:80
k port-forward svc/service-name 8080:80
```

Background:
```bash
k port-forward svc/db 5432:5432 &
```

## Copy files
```bash
k cp pod-name:/tmp/file.txt ./file.txt
k cp ./local.txt pod-name:/tmp/
```

## Dry-run
```bash
k apply -f file.yaml --dry-run=client -o yaml
```

See what would be created.

## Diff
```bash
k diff -f file.yaml
```

See difference between file y cluster state.

## Bulk operations

### Delete all pods matching label
```bash
k delete pods -l app=my-app
```

### Delete stuck pods
```bash
k delete pods --field-selector status.phase=Failed
```

### Restart deployment
```bash
k rollout restart deployment/my-app
```

## kubectl config

### Ver contextos
```bash
k config get-contexts
```

### Ver current config
```bash
k config view
```

### Merge kubeconfigs
```bash
KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config1:~/.kube/config2 k config view --flatten > ~/.kube/merged
```

## Aliases más avanzados
```bash
alias klf='k logs -f'
alias kgp='k get pods'
alias kgs='k get svc'
alias kgn='k get nodes'
alias kgd='k get deployments'
alias kwatch='watch -n 1 kubectl get pods'
alias k9s='k9s'    # TUI dashboard
```

## k9s (TUI dashboard)
```bash
brew install k9s
k9s
```

Terminal UI para navegar cluster interactively. Ver pods, deployments, nodes con hotkeys.

## Common issues

### 'Context not found'
- Config file en `~/.kube/config`
- Add context via CLI o cloud provider (aws eks update-kubeconfig, etc.)

### 'Slow autocomplete'
- Too many resources
- Cache local

### 'Permission denied'
- RBAC missing
- Check: `k auth can-i list pods`

## Cheat sheet
SAP-esque quick reference:
- `k get pods` — list pods
- `k describe pod X` — details
- `k logs X` — logs
- `k exec X -it -- bash` — shell
- `k apply -f file` — create/update
- `k delete -f file` — remove
- `k edit deployment X` — edit inline
- `k scale deployment X --replicas=3` — scale
- `k rollout status deployment/X` — check rollout
- `k rollout undo deployment/X` — rollback

## Best practices
- **Alias everything** — save keystrokes
- **Autocomplete** on
- **kubectx/kubens** — no manual context switching
- **k9s or stern** — visualize efficiently
- **`-o` variants** — right output format for task
- **RBAC check first** before troubleshooting
